topics.title: Walk through SOLID tied to React.
topics.html:
• S — Single Responsibility. UserCard renders, not fetches. useUserData is a separate hook.
  • O — Open/Closed. New Button variant = pass variant='danger', not add an if inside.
  • L — Liskov. PrimaryButton works wherever Button is expected without breaking the contract.
  • I — Interface Segregation. Several narrow prop interfaces beat one wide monster.
  • D — Dependency Inversion. Component takes onFetch: () => Promise as prop, not imports axios directly.
// DIP — depend on abstraction
function DataWidget<T>({ fetchFn }: { fetchFn: () => Promise<T> }) {
  const { data } = useQuery(["w"], fetchFn);
  return <pre>{JSON.stringify(data)}</pre>;
}
// Prod: <DataWidget fetchFn={() => api.getMetrics()} />
// Test: <DataWidget fetchFn={() => Promise.resolve(mock)} />
💬 Say it like this

I think about SOLID in terms of React patterns. Single responsibility: a component either displays data or fetches it — not both. Open/Closed: adding a new button style should be a new prop value, not a new if-statement. Dependency Inversion: a component should receive its data source as a prop — this is why testability improves so much when you pass fetchFn instead of calling api.get directly.

topics.title: Immutability — why critical in React?
topics.html:
// BAD — same ref, no re-render
items[0].name = "B"; setItems(items);
// GOOD — new reference
setItems(prev => prev.map(i => i.id === 1 ? { ...i, name: "B" } : i));
// Immer
import { produce } from "immer";
setItems(produce(draft => { draft[0].name = "B"; }));
💬 Say it like this

React compares state by reference, not by content. If I change an object in place, the reference stays the same, React sees nothing new, and the component does not re-render.

So I always create a new object or a new array — spread, map, filter. On deeply nested state I use Immer, which lets me write it like a mutation while it produces a new object underneath.
